concepts.def: The drive that makes people work harder/better
Basic needs: food, water, rest (Maslow level 1)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Maslow stacks needs: physiological → safety → social → esteem → self-actualisation.

You can't motivate with esteem if basic needs (wages, breaks) aren't met first.

Herzberg split motivation into two sets.

Hygiene factors (pay, conditions, supervision) only PREVENT unhappiness. Motivators (achievement, recognition, growth) actually drive performance.

A manager who gives a pay rise but no praise (Herzberg) may still see flat motivation.

Maslow says: meet the level that's missing — don't just add more of what's already there.

What is a key disadvantage of being a sole trader?
options: Sole traders must employ at least one other person by law.
Unlimited liability — the owner's personal assets are at risk if the business fails, because there is no legal separation between owner and business.
The main disadvantage is that sole traders can't sell any products.
A brand is the company that makes a product.

mcqs.q: What is Taylor's theory of scientific management?
options: A brand is the company that makes a product.
Workers are motivated primarily by money; efficiency is maximised by breaking tasks into standardised steps, training workers in 'the one best way', and using piece-rate pay.
Taylor said workers are motivated by recognition and teamwork.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
